title: From every nation, a group gathered and driven.
subtitle: Deniers brought forward on the Day
then: Ibn Kathir describes {trap}the wrongdoers who disbelieved in the signs and Messengers being gathered before Allah{/trap}, a group from every people and generation. He links it to the verse about the wrongdoers being assembled with their companions.
now: Who you spend your evenings with shapes who you become. The friends you laugh with at wrong things. {idea}On that Day, people stand with their kind.{/idea} You can choose your company now.
old: Who I hang out with does not change who I am.
new: I will be gathered with the people I chose to walk with, so I should choose well.
try: Spend time today with one person who reminds you of Allah.

title: You denied what you never understood?
subtitle: The question at the place of reckoning
then: Ibn Kathir explains that standing before Allah, {trap}they will be asked about their beliefs and their deeds.{/trap} The question points out they rejected signs they never tried to understand.
now: You dismissed something about faith because of a meme, a bad experience, a headline. {trap}You rejected it without ever studying it.{/trap} The question will be: did you even look? And what did you do?
old: I can dismiss what I have not studied if it does not feel right.
new: I will be asked whether I really looked before I rejected, and what I did with what I knew.
try: Pick one question about your faith you have avoided. Look up a reliable answer today.

title: No excuse left, and no words to say.
subtitle: Speechless before the One who sees
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they will be stunned and speechless, unable to give any answer{/trap}, because they wronged themselves in the world and have now returned to the One from Whom nothing is hidden. He cites the verse that they will not be permitted to give excuses.
now: You have a ready explanation for most things: tired, busy, stressed, everyone does it. {idea}Excuses work on people.{/idea} The time to fix things is while words can still turn into change.
old: I will be able to explain my reasons when the time comes.
new: The time for explaining and changing is now, not on the Day.
try: Drop one excuse you use often. Do the thing instead, once, today.

title: Night for rest, day for sight.
subtitle: A daily sign everyone lives inside
then: Between scenes of the Day, Allah points to everyday life. Ibn Kathir explains the darkness of night lets people {reward}halt their activities and calm down to recover from the day{/reward}, and day is filled with light so they can {reward}work, travel and earn a living.{/reward}
now: You scroll in bed until 2am, then drag yourself through the morning. {idea}Night was made for rest.{/idea} Respecting the rhythm Allah made is a kind of gratitude.
old: Night is just extra time for screens.
new: Night and day are signs made for my rest and my work, and I can honor both.
try: Put your phone away 30 minutes earlier tonight and rest.

title: The Horn is blown, and all come humbled.
subtitle: The Day everyone answers the call
then: Ibn Kathir says the Horn will be blown by the angel Israfil, {trap}signaling the end of this world.{/trap} Everyone will be terrified except whom Allah wills, which he says are {reward}the martyrs, alive with their Lord.{/reward} All come to Him {idea}humbling themselves and obeying.{/idea}
now: You flinch at a loud alarm, a sudden siren on the street. Imagine a sound that stops every phone, every meeting, every argument at once. {idea}Every person walking toward Him, humbled.{/idea} Humility now is practice for then.
old: Some people are too important to be humbled.
new: Everyone will come to Allah humbled, so I can choose humility now.
try: In your next sajdah, stay a few extra seconds and feel how small you are before Him.

title: Mountains that seem fixed will drift like clouds.
subtitle: Nothing solid stays forever
then: Ibn Kathir explains you see the mountains {idea}as if they are fixed and will remain{/idea}, but they will move like clouds. It is the work of Allah who perfected all He created, and {idea}He knows all His servants do, good or evil.{/idea}
now: Your career, your house, the life you have built: it all feels like a mountain. {idea}Even mountains will drift.{/idea} The only thing that lasts is what you did, which He already knows.
old: The solid things in my life will always be there.
new: Even what seems most permanent will pass, so I should invest in what lasts.
try: Look at the sky or a hill today and remind yourself it will pass, but your deeds remain.

title: Bring good, receive better, and be safe.
subtitle: The reward for sincere good
then: Qatadah said the good deed is {idea}sincerely for Allah alone.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes Allah explained elsewhere that {reward}He will give ten like it{/reward}, and that such people will be safe from the terror of that Day, untouched by the greatest terror.
now: You helped a neighbor carry groceries. You paid for a stranger's coffee. You held your tongue when you wanted to snap. {reward}Done for Allah, each one comes back multiplied.{/reward} And on the hardest Day, it becomes safety.
old: Small good deeds do not add up to much.
new: Every sincere good deed comes back better and brings me safety on the Day.
try: Do one small good deed today purely for Allah, and tell no one.

title: Repaid only for what you used to do.
subtitle: The other side of the scale
then: Ibn Kathir says this is for {trap}whoever comes to Allah with evil deeds and no good deeds, or whose evil outweighs their good.{/trap} They are told: {idea}are you being repaid for anything except what you used to do?{/idea}
now: The habit you keep returning to. The person you keep hurting. {idea}What you used to do is what you will meet.{/idea} The hopeful side: you can start adding good to the scale today.
old: My bad habits are small and will not really count against me.
new: I will meet exactly what I used to do, so I can start changing the balance now.
try: Pair one bad habit with one good deed today, every time it shows up.

title: I am only commanded to worship the Lord of this city.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ states his mission
then: Ibn Kathir says linking Lord to this city is {reward}a sign of honor and divine care{/reward} for Makkah. He cites the Prophet ﷺ on the day of the conquest: {idea}this city was made sacred by Allah the day He created the heavens and the earth.{/idea}
now: You face the qiblah five times a day, from your bedroom, your office, an airport corner. {idea}Your direction points to one sacred city, but the Lord of it owns everything.{/idea} Your whole life is His.
old: Worship is for the mosque and special places.
new: The Lord of the sacred city owns everything, so every part of my life is for Him.
try: At your next prayer, pause as you face the qiblah and remember who owns everything.

title: Recite it. Guidance helps the one who takes it.
subtitle: The warner's job, and its limit
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to recite the Quran to people {idea}so as to convey it{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says he had an example in the Messengers who warned their people, and Allah would do the judging, as another verse says: {idea}your duty is only to convey.{/idea}
now: You share a verse in the family group, give a gentle reminder at dinner. Some respond, some roll their eyes. {idea}Your part is to say it well.{/idea} What they do with it is between them and Allah.
old: If people do not change after I remind them, I have failed.
new: My job is to convey kindly; guidance benefits whoever accepts it.
try: Share one verse you love with someone today, with no expectation.

title: Praise Allah. You will see His signs.
subtitle: How the surah closes
then: The surah ends with praise to Allah, {idea}who does not punish anyone except after establishing proof and warning.{/idea} He will show His signs. Ibn Kathir notes Imam Ahmad used to recite: {idea}if you are alone one day, do not say I am alone; say someone is watching me.{/idea}
now: Late at night, the house quiet, phone in hand, no one around. {idea}You are never really alone.{/idea} That is not a threat. It is the closing comfort of a surah full of His signs.
old: When no one is around, what I do does not really matter.
new: Allah is never unaware of me, and I will keep recognizing His signs if I look.
try: Tonight, when you are alone, say al-hamdu lillah and remember He is with you.
